# Day-over-day OI change — 2026-07-09 → 2026-07-10

Input to the Phase-2 detection design session: what day-over-day OI-change signal do Schwab
chain snapshots support? OI is settled once daily and static intraday (2026-07-06 measured 0
intraday OI changes), so each day's last snapshot is that session's settled OI.

This is the **canonical consecutive-pair** run (7/9 → 7/10, both captured ~19:56–19:59 UTC),
matching production's nightly cadence (ADR-0020). The earlier 7/6 → 7/9 run was a plumbing
smoke-test only (3-session cumulative delta).

## What the deltas support (session takeaways)

1. **The consecutive-pair delta is clean and large enough to detect on.** Shared contracts
   dominate every book (single-cycle names: 100% shared, 0 vanished); 1,100–2,700 contracts per
   underlying moved OI day-over-day, with top single-contract moves of +5k to +28k — far above
   noise.
2. **OI timing semantics (PIT rule for the detector):** day D's settled OI reflects positioning
   as of D−1's close — this 7/9→7/10 delta measures *net position change from trading on 7/9*.
   Day-2 confirmation of day-1 flow is exactly the lag ADR-0020's nightly capture provides;
   intraday flow (volume/IV) leads, OI confirms one session later.
3. **Build vs. unwind is the dimension intraday snapshots cannot give.** 5-min volume deltas
   can't distinguish opening from closing trades (no aggressor side at REST cadence); the OI
   delta's sign does. Example — NVDA (+3.6% day): calls at/above the new price built massively
   (207.5C +19.1k, 205C +18.9k, 210C +16.5k = new opened interest chasing the move) while the
   crossed 197.5C unwound −13.8k (closed/rolled ahead of expiry). That build/unwind split against
   the underlying's move is the day-2 confirmation signal.
4. **Net must be computed over the *shared* roster, not book totals.** For daily/weekly-expiry
   ETFs the expiry churn is material (SPY: 334 vanished, shared-net +603k vs book-net +267k;
   QQQ: 366 vanished, +430k vs +66k). Book-total OI change conflates expiry roll-off with new
   positioning.
5. **Strike-listing churn tracks the move.** New strikes appear where price went (AMD +520
   contracts listed after its +2.1% day; META +340 after +6.0%) — `appeared` contracts have no
   early-side OI by definition, so they enter the delta universe one session later.
